RULES (FOLLOW THESE STRICTLY):
1. TENSE & VOICE (MANDATORY): Every sentence MUST be in past tense and passive voice. Change verbs: "start" -> "was started", "administer" -> "was administered", "obtain" -> "was obtained", "refer" -> "was referred", "consult" -> "was consulted". Do NOT use present tense ("is given", "are ordered") or imperative mood.
2. COMPLETENESS (MOST IMPORTANT): Include every clinically relevant detail from the orders: medications (dose, route, frequency), diagnostics, fluids, diet, oxygen and ventilator settings, labs, procedures, referrals, held or discontinued items, PRN conditions, monitoring, consult criteria. Orders continued from previous days are details too: name each with its dose in one sentence (e.g. "Drug A 500 mg IV q8h and Drug B 10 mg 1 tab OD were continued."), never just "medications were continued". Mention supplies and materials only when truly essential (e.g. a blood product or device used on the patient); otherwise just name the procedure they are for.

Aim for about 5 sentences; when the orders need more, add sentences instead of lengthening them, and keep each sentence under about 35 words. Do not use bullet points or numbered lists.

The patient was referred to Neurosurgery for co-management and a repeat plain cranial CT scan was requested. For subarachnoid hemorrhage with intraventricular extension from a ruptured left MCA aneurysm, present management and medical decompression were continued with adequate NPO. Aneurysmal clipping was tentatively scheduled for the next afternoon, with the OR and Anesthesia informed, consent secured, the main service informed and cardiopulmonary clearance secured. A surgical assist was referred, non-institutional labs were uploaded to the EMR, and Neurosurgery was informed of the surgical plan.

Creatinine was added to the labs and Totilac was increased to 50 cc/hr. PNSS 1 L x 80 cc/hr and OF 1200 kcal Boost Optimum in 6 divided feedings were given. The nicardipine drip was off, and mannitol 100 cc q6h, nimodipine 30 mg 2 tabs q4h and edaravone 30 mg IV q12h were continued. Telmisartan 40 mg OD, carvedilol 12.5 mg BID, paracetamol 600 mg IV q6h RTC and levetiracetam 500 mg 1 tab BID were continued. Ketorolac 30 mg IV q8h PRN, metoclopramide 10 mg IV q8h PRN, omeprazole 40 mg IV q12h and NAC 600 mg 1 tab OD were continued. A side drip of PNSS 100 cc + 40 mEq KCl at 4 mEq/hr was started. Left pterional craniotomy with clipping of the left posterior communicating artery aneurysm was scheduled that afternoon, with 2 units pRBC secured and STAT PT/PTT. The family was told that the goal was to prevent re-rupture, and of the risks of infection, bleeding including intra-op rupture, worsening vasospasm and cerebral injury. The operating microscope was confirmed. Risk stratification showed RCRI 5% (intermediate cardiac risk), ARISCAT 13.3% (high pulmonary risk) and elevated bleeding risk, and the risks were explained to the family. CBG q4h while on NPO was ordered, with BP kept at 120-140 mmHg during the procedure and underhydration avoided. Blood typing was done and the PT/PTT was followed up. Serum sodium was monitored q8h, nimodipine 60 mg q4h, mannitol 100 ml q6h, Totilac, edaravone IV q12h and levetiracetam 500 mg BID were continued. The patient was watched for neurologic deterioration and new focal deficits, with urine output and fluid balance monitored and SBP kept at 100-120 mmHg. Totilac was decreased to 40 cc/hr and the family was told of the risk of vasospasm. Prosec was used for omeprazole and Kenzipine for nicardipine. Zynapse 1 g IV q8h was started, targeting SBP below 140 mmHg pre-op and 150-160 mmHg post-op. After left pterional craniotomy with clipping and lumbar drain insertion under GETA with scalp block, the patient was transferred to the MICU. MV was reconnected on AC mode, TV 380, BUR 16, I:E 1:2.5, with ABG after 30 minutes. The lumbar drain and NGT were maintained, the patient was kept NPO except for oral medications via NGT, and moderate high backrest was kept with the head midline at 30 degrees. IVF was PNSS 1 L x 120 cc/hr, PLRS 1 L x 120 cc/hr and PNSS 1 L x 110 cc/hr. Paracetamol 1 g IV q6h x 4 more doses was given, then 600 mg IV q6h RTC, with ketorolac 30 mg IV q6h x 5 doses. Fentanyl 50 mcg IV q4h x 2 doses, then q4h PRN, and ondansetron 4 mg IV q8h x 2 doses were given. Ceftriaxone 2 g IV OD was started, and Totilac 40 cc/hr and levetiracetam 500 mg q12h per NGT were continued. Diazepam 5 mg IV was on standby for frank seizures (maximum 30 mg). Omeprazole 40 mg IV OD and nimodipine 30 mg 2 caps q4h were continued. SBP was strictly kept at 150-160 mmHg, avoiding hypotension (target MAP 80-100), and all antihypertensives were held. Post-op CBC, Na, K, Cl, iCa, Mg and creatinine and serial serum sodium q8h were requested. Chlorhexidine gargle 15-20 ml TID was started. Vital signs were taken q15 minutes x 1 hour then hourly, with urine output recorded q1h and CBG q6h while on NPO. The elastic bandage, dressing and staples were maintained with daily neck flat dressing, watching for soaked dressing, profuse bleeding and fever. Mannitol was discontinued, with a BP target of 150-170 mmHg and Na target of 150-155. Norepinephrine (Norkenz) 8 mg in 100 cc PNSS was allowed to augment BP. Totilac was continued at 40 cc/hr. For hypokalemia (deficit 66), a KCl side drip of 40 mEq in 100 cc PNSS at 4 mEq/hr was given for 1 more cycle. All antihypertensives (telmisartan, carvedilol) stayed on hold.
